label: Proposition E
title: City Administrator’s Authority and Changes to City Contracting
q: Shall the City amend the Charter to give the City Administrator more authority by centralizing the City’s purchasing rules and processes, changing how the City approves purchasing rules, changing when contracts and leases require Board of Supervisors approval, and extending the City Administrator’s term?
now: The City Administrator’s Office is responsible for most of the City’s purchasing. However, authority for the City’s purchasing and technology is shared among the City Administrator’s Office, the Board of Supervisors, the Mayor, and some City departments.${F(1)}
does:
Proposition E would:
• Rules Regulating Purchasing: Give the City Administrator exclusive authority to propose ordinances that change how the City selects contractors and enters into contracts for goods, services, construction, and grants (Purchasing).${F(1)}
yes: If you vote “yes,” you want to give the City Administrator more authority by centralizing the City’s Purchasing rules and processes, changing how the City approves Purchasing rules, changing when contracts and leases require Board approval, and extending the City Administrator’s term.
no: If you vote “no,” you do not want to make these changes.

1: Official Voter Information Guide, San Francisco, Nov. 3, 2026, pp. 94 to 95
